context:
No nightly job, as you asked. `make backup` runs the backup once; only a separate command installs the nightly job.
The iCloud folder is empty today, so a first run overwrites nothing. The risk starts at the second run: today a changed or corrupted photo replaces the good copy, and the store copy is replaced each run with no check.
The guard is three changes in one script:
- A photo already backed up is never overwritten. A difference is counted and reported.
- Each store copy is dated and kept, and checked for corruption before it lands.
- A verify pass compares every file's fingerprint, source against backup (one read of 7.9 GB).
Cost: about 0.16 GB per store copy kept. A real re-shoot shows as 'differs' until you accept it.

options.gain: A copy exists today. The first run cannot overwrite anything.
options.how: Run `make backup` once today, then one builder lane adds all three changes before any second run.
options.label: Back up now, build the guard next
options.lose: This first copy is not fingerprint-checked until the verify pass lands.

options.gain: The first copy is checked from the start.
options.how: One builder lane adds all three changes; the backup runs once after it merges.
options.label: Build the guard, then back up
options.lose: No backup exists until the lane merges.

options.how: Build only the never-overwrite and dated-store changes, then back up once.
options.label: Guard without the verify pass
options.lose: No way to prove the backup matches your photos.

ref: lean-server spec section 6; DEBT67, capture photographs exist in one place
title: One-time backup: run it now, or after the guard is built?
why: The first run is safe because the folder is empty, so waiting buys nothing. The guard matters only from the second run on.
